_note: Claims for elon-time.html, drawn by assets/home/claims.js. Any order; the page sorts by date said. Every entry marked placeholder is a sample written to fill the layout: replace them with the real list and delete the flag. Field guide at the bottom of this file.

claims.title: Coast-to-coast self-driving demo
claims.where: Tesla press call on new Autopilot hardware
claims.quote: We’ll be able to do a demonstration drive of full autonomy all the way from LA to New York by the end of next year.
claims.outcome: No Tesla has made the drive without a human in charge. Full Self-Driving is still sold as a supervised system.

claims.title: People on the way to Mars
claims.quote: If things go super well, we could see the first crewed flight to Mars in about 2024.
claims.outcome: Starship is still flying suborbital and orbital tests. No crewed or uncrewed mission has left for Mars.

claims.title: Tesla Semi in production
claims.quote: Production of the Semi begins in 2019.
claims.outcome: The first handful of trucks went to PepsiCo in December 2022. Volume production was still being set up years later.

claims.title: The new Roadster
claims.quote: The new Roadster will be available in 2020.
claims.outcome: Customers paid deposits of up to $250,000. No production Roadster has been delivered.

claims.title: “Funding secured”
claims.quote: Am considering taking Tesla private at $420. Funding secured.
claims.outcome: There was no firm funding. The SEC charged Musk with fraud; he and Tesla each paid $20 million and he stepped down as chairman.

claims.title: A million robotaxis
claims.quote: Next year for sure, we will have over a million robotaxis on the road.
claims.outcome: Tesla began a small paid service in Austin in June 2025, with a safety monitor in each car. The fleet is in the dozens, not the millions.

claims.title: Cybertruck on the road
claims.quote: Production is expected to begin in late 2021.
claims.outcome: The first trucks were handed over at a launch event in Texas on 30 November 2023.

claims.title: A $39,900 Cybertruck
claims.outcome: At launch the cheapest version was listed at $60,990, and it was not due until 2025.

claims.title: Covid cases near zero
claims.quote: Based on current trends, probably close to zero new cases in US too by end of April.
claims.outcome: The US was still recording around 30,000 new cases a day at the end of April 2020.

claims.title: 500,000 cars in 2018
claims.quote: We’re going to try to get to 500,000 total vehicle production in 2018.
claims.outcome: Tesla built about half that. It first passed 500,000 in a year in 2020.

_fields.id: Short slug, unique. Becomes the link anchor, e.g. elon-time.html#million-robotaxis.
_fields.title: Four or five words for the timeline label.
_fields.company: Free text. Each distinct value becomes a filter: Tesla, SpaceX, X, Neuralink, The Boring Company, DOGE, Personal…
_fields.kind: deadline (a promise with a date), false (a statement that wasn't true) or figure (a number that came out wrong).
_fields.said: When he said it: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY.
_fields.where: Where he said it: an event, a call, a platform.
_fields.quote: His words, without quotation marks. The page adds them.
_fields.due: deadline only. The date he gave. YYYY means the end of that year, YYYY-MM the end of that month.
_fields.delivered: deadline only. When it actually happened, or null if it still hasn't.
_fields.unit: figure only. "$" goes before the number; anything else (cars, people, %) goes after it.
_fields.claimed / actual: figure only. { value, label } for what he said and what happened. The page draws them to scale.
_fields.outcome: One or two sentences on what happened.
_fields.sources: List of { label, url }. Shown under each entry.
_fields.placeholder: true marks a sample entry. The page shows a note while any remain.
